note: A fleet is a group of AI agents launched together in one build session for one mission; standing entries are always-on automation, runs are dated launches.

runs.name: Estate ops fleet
runs.mission: Execute the operator queue in order: ship the portal, stage the Season Zero commitment, prove pin parity at scale, clean up, audit DNS, fix site vulnerabilities.

agents.brief: Merge the portal PR, watch the production deploy, verify the live bundle and headers.
Generate the commitment package, verify it three independent ways, stage the backups — stop at the operator's signature line.
Attempt the 10,000-file sharding parity pin against the pin service.
Read-only DNSSEC and CAA posture audit of mergedpublic.com with an ordered enablement plan.
Fix the site's open Dependabot security alerts on a reviewed branch.

outcomes: The build transparency portal is LIVE at mergedpublic.com/build — PR #41 merged, the deploy succeeded, and the new bundle and security headers were verified serving in production.

The Season Zero commitment package is generated and hash-verified three independent ways; it now waits only on the operator's offline backup, the manifest commit, and the treasury echo (no clue drops before then).
The 10,000-file parity pin was REFUSED by the pin service's free-tier file cap — a paid pinning plan is now a confirmed hard prerequisite for reveal week, recorded in MP-REVEAL.md.

DNS posture established read-only: DNS on Azure DNS, registrar GoDaddy, DNSSEC off, no CAA records; an ordered enablement plan was delivered to the operator (CAA first, then zone signing, then the DS record).

All four open Dependabot alerts on the website (1 high, 3 moderate — vite and esbuild) are fixed in PR #42 with a clean build and zero audit findings; left open for human review because the fix requires a vite 5-to-6 major jump.
The wedged workflow run is still queued at GitHub and was left untouched; its authorized deletion waits until GitHub marks it completed.

runs.name: Build portal fleet
runs.mission: Ship the merged transparency portal: the data spine in this repo plus the pages that render it on mergedpublic.com/build.

agents.brief: Author portal/status.json, portal/fleets.json, the letters index, and the feature-request intake in this public repo.
Build the /build pages on mergedpublic.com that fetch and render this data.
Adversarial check of data accuracy, schema agreement between the two repos, and compliance language.

outcomes: The data spine went live in this repo (portal/, letters/ with letter 001, the feature-request intake) on 2026-08-19.
The /build portal shipped as merged-website PR #41, awaiting the operator's merge — merge is the ship decision.
Three adversarial verifiers filed findings (a mislabeled request-form URL, unlabeled session-updated stats, a self-contradicting correction policy, and more) — all fixed before the PR opened.

runs.name: MP Phase A build fleet
runs.mission: Build and adversarially verify the Merged Public assignment engine, public verifier, and reveal pin tooling ahead of the Season Zero commitment.

agents.brief: Assignment engine — stays private until reveal by design (MP-REVEAL.md).
Public verifier (verify-mp) — holds no secrets, public from day one.
Directory-scale pin tool for the reveal image and metadata trees.
USDG-revoke and manifest-echo scripts for the operator to sign.
Determinism re-run — engine output must be bit-for-bit repeatable.
Mutation tests — the verifier must catch deliberately corrupted sets.
Script safety review of everything the operator will be asked to sign.

outcomes: Gate A passed: three fresh-process engine runs byte-identical, and an independent verifier reproduced the output byte-for-byte.
The public verifier generator/merged-public/verify-mp.mjs shipped — it caught 8 of 8 deliberately corrupted assignment sets in mutation testing and passes live against the on-chain provenance hash.
The directory-scale pin tool proved its core guarantee on a real test pin: the locally computed directory CID matched the pin service's byte-for-byte.
The script-safety verifier found real defects in the operator scripts (a key-echoing error path, silent unknown-flag fallthrough) — closed by the hardening fleet the same day.

runs.name: MP scripts hardening fleet
runs.mission: Close the nine findings from the Phase A script-safety review and prove each one closed by independent re-execution, not by trusting the fixer.

agents.brief: Apply the enumerated hardening list to the owner scripts, the pin tool, the public verifier, and the commitment script.
Re-demonstrate every finding closed: fake-key leak probes on every failure path, misspelled-flag refusals before any network call, sample-selection proofs.

outcomes: All nine findings closed: key handling is value-free on every failure path, unknown flags refuse before any network or key handling, and the reveal verification sample always includes tokens 1 and 10000.
Regression sweep clean: the live allowance report, the deterministic pin dry-run, and the public verifier all still pass.

runs.name: Six-lane estate audit
runs.mission: Audit the whole estate — contracts, keys, website, and operations — across six lanes and record every finding.

agents.brief: One audit lane each across the estate; findings recorded in SECURITY.md and the session report.

outcomes: Website hardening shipped: CSP, HSTS, robots, worker origin gate (merged-website PR #33).
Open finding recorded in SECURITY.md: an unlimited USDG allowance from the operator wallet to a shared Seaport conduit; revoke pending an operator signature.
